body: Once per turn, unless this model is fleeing or engaged in combat, a single friendly Slann Mage-Priest that is within 24" of this model may ‘channel’ a spell through this model.

If they do, the range (including the range to dispel unless it is a vortex), targeting restrictions and all effects of the spell are measured from this model, rather than from the caster. If the spell requires a line of sight, it is determined from this model.

Models with this special rule treat terrain designated as a ‘water feature’ as Open Ground. In addition, as long as at least 50% of the models in the unit are within a ‘water feature’ they benefit from partial cover. ‘Water features’ might include shallow streams or fords, swampy ground, fast flowing rivers, ponds or lakes, and players should agree prior to the game if any terrain is a water feature.
Each war beast in a unit with this special rule is accompanied by a number of models representing its handlers. As long as any handlers remain, the war beast ignores the Undisciplined special rule.
During deployment, position these models anywhere within 1” of the war beasts. If the handlers are found to be blocking movement or line of sight, simply move them aside.

In combat, each handler adds its attacks to those of the war beasts. If there are multiple war beasts in combat, the additional attacks from the handlers are distributed as evenly as possible among the war beasts.

If a war beast suffers an unsaved wound from any source, roll a D6. On a roll of 1-4 a war beast loses a Wound, but on a roll of 5+ one of the handlers is removed instead. If all war beasts are removed from play, so are the handlers.

A model with this special rule (but not its mount) generates one additional Attack on any natural roll of a 6 made when rolling To Hit in close combat. Roll To Hit and To Wound for this additional Attack as normal. Additional Attacks generated by this special rule cannot themselves generate further Attacks.
When required to make a Leadership or Break Test, models with this special rule may roll an extra D6 and discard the highest result.

Once per game, a unit with this special rule may perform a ‘Drop Rocks’ attack against a single enemy unit that is not engaged in combat. To do so, this unit must move (by flying) over the unit it wishes to attack during the Remaining Moves sub-phase. Once this unit’s movement is complete, the enemy unit suffers D3 Strength 4 hits, each with an AP of -1, for each model in this unit that moved over it.
Blessed by Itzl, skinks are cunning riders, and let their ferocious mounts do the brunt of the fighting
Attacks made against this unit are resolved against the weapon skill of the rider, the crew, or monster, whichever is higher.

Once per turn, the Slann Mage-Priest may re-roll one of the D6 when making a Casting Roll. This ability may not be used to re-roll a Miscast. In addition, it knows one more spell (chosen in the usual way) than is normal for their Level of Wizardry.

This character may join a unit with the Guardians special rule despite having the Fly special rule. As long as the front rank has a minimum of 4 models they must be placed in the second rank. However, they continue to confer benefits to the unit in the form of Leadership and Special Rules. As long as this model is not in base to base contact with an enemy model, they do not count as being in a fighting rank and they may cast and dispel as normal, even if its unit is engaged in Combat. However, it may not cast Assailment spells.

If the model with this rule is unable to fit neatly into the unit, count its base size as if it were on the correct base size for all purposes for as long as it remains in the unit. IE: a Mage-Priest (50mm x 50mm) counts as having a base of 60mm x 60mm when it joins a unit of Temple Guard (30mm x 30mm). To achieve this, you may use a spacer, or simply leave room to either side of its base on the movement tray so that rear ranks can close around it correctly.

When a unit of Skink Cohorts that includes Kroxigor deploys or reforms, the Kroxigor must be placed in the unit’s second rank, as close to the centre of the rank as possible. If there is not enough room in the second rank for all Kroxigor models to fit, any remaining models are placed in the immediate ranks behind and in contact with another Kroxigor. If at any time there are not enough models in the unit to form a second rank, the Kroxigors must immediately join the front rank.
Kroxigor that have joined a unit of Skinks are affected by enemy shooting in the same way as described under Enemy Shooting (Characters) Rulebook, p.209.

In combat, if a Kroxigor is in base contact with a Skink of its own unit which in turn is in base contact with an enemy model, then the Kroxigor too is counted as being in base contact with that enemy model and vice versa. Therefore, the Kroxigor is part of the fighting rank, and both the Kroxigor and enemy model can direct their full number of attacks against, or divide them between any models that they are in base contact with in this way. However, Kroxigor can only have Impact Hits or Stomp Attacks directed against them if there are fewer than five rank and file Skink models in the unit. A Kroxigor that is not in base contact with an enemy model in this way, but is in base contact with a Skink model in a fighting rank that can fight, may make a single attack.

Wounds inflicted on the Kroxigor are lost by a single model until its Wounds characteristic is reduced to zero. Wounds are then lost by the next Kroxigor, and so on. Excess wounds inflicted upon the Skink unit do not 'spill over' onto the Kroxigor that have joined it, and vice versa.
Any enemy model that shoots at a unit with this rule suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

This unit may be joined by a character with the Palanquin special rule. In addition, any model in a unit of Temple Guard that contains a Slann Mage-Priest can issue and accept challenges in the same manner as a character.

Before the game starts, but after Scouts have been deployed, you may place one Lustrian blot toad marker for each unit of Ripperdactyl Riders in your army (counting only units, not including characters mounted on Ripperdactyls). A single blot toad marker can be placed on any enemy unit on the battlefield, this marker remains throughout the battle.
When engaged in combat with an enemy unit with a blot toad marker, Ripperdactyls (but not their riders) gain the Extra Attacks (1), and the Hatred (blot toad marker) special rules
An Ancient Stegadon equipped with an Engine of the Gods gains the following special rules:

rows: Friendly models that cast a Bound spell whilst within 12" of one or more Engine of the Gods may apply a +1 modifier to the Casting roll.

body: An Engine of the Gods can cast the following Bound spells, with a Power Level of 2:
Burning Alignment:
Effect: The target enemy unit suffers 2D6 Strength 4 hits, each with an AP of -. This Bound spell has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

Effect: Remains in Play. Whilst this Bound spell is in play, this model and any friendly unit within 12" of this model gains a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered. However, if this model casts the Burning Alignment Bound spell, this Bound spell will immediately expire.
A Bastiladon equipped with an Ark of Sotek gains the following special rules:
Slithering Serpents: During the Shooting phase, every enemy unit within D6" of this model suffers 2D6 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of - with the Poison Attacks special rule.
Spawn of Sotek: During the Command sub-phase of its turn, roll a D6. On a roll of 4+, a single Jungle Swarm within 6" of this model regains D3 lost Wounds .

Once per game, during the Command sub-phase of their turn, this model may attempt to unleash the primeval savagery of the Lizardmen by making a Leadership test (using its own Leadership). If this test is passed, until the end of that turn all friendly Lizardmen units with the Predatory Fighter special rule within 8" of this model gain an additional attack on any successful To Hit roll of a 5 or a 6 until the end of the turn.

Effect: This spell can only target friendly characters but may target characters engaged in combat. If this spell is cast with a casting result of 8 or more, the target friendly model immediately regains 1 lost Wound. If this spell is cast with a casting result of 10 or more, the target friendly model immediately regains D3 lost Wounds.
In addition, the target friendly character gains the Fear special rule. If they already have the Fear special rule, they instead gain the Terror special rule.

Effect: Remains in play. Place a large (5") blast template so that its central hole is within 18" of the caster. Whilst in play, the template is treated as a ‘water feature’ that is dangerous terrain over which no line of sight can be drawn. During every Start of Turn sub-phase (see page 95) the template may move D6" in a direction of the caster’s choosing. Any enemy unit that moves through the template, or that the template moves over becomes 'drenched' for as long as this spell remains in play .

A drenched unit suffers a -1 To Hit modifier during the Shooting phase. A drenched model whose troop type is ‘war machine’ must roll a D6 before shooting. On a roll of 3 or less the model fails to shoot this turn.

A Slann Mage-Priest may purchase up to three Disciplines of the Old Ones. Each Discipline may only be taken once per army.

shield-of-the-mirror-pool.body: The Shield of the Mirror Pool is a shield. In addition, any magic missile that strikes the bearer or any unit he is with is reflected on the roll of 4+ on a D6. If the spell is reflected, the caster (and their unit) become the target of the spell. The caster may make a Wizardly dispel attempt.

sun-standard-of-chotec.body: Enemy units cannot declare a Stand & Shoot charge reaction against a unit carrying the Sun Standard of Chotec. In addition, enemy models suffer a -1 modifier on any To Hit rolls made against the unit carrying this banner.

jaguar-standard.body: When a unit carrying the Jaguar Standard makes a Pursuit or Charge roll, it may roll an extra D6 and discard the lowest result.

venom-of-the-firefly-frog.body:
All attacks made during the Combat phase by the bearer of the Venom of the Firefly Frog have the Poisoned Attacks and Magical Attacks special rules.

Note that this only applies to non-magical weapons and does not apply to a model’s mount (should it have one).

itxi-grub.body: Single use. Before making a Casting roll, the bearer may attempt to consume a single Itxi Grub by making a Leadership test using their own Leadership. If this test is passed, the bearer may apply a +3 modifier to the Casting roll.

higher-state-of-consciousness.body: This character gains the Ethereal special rule.

focus-of-mystery.body:
This Character does not randomly generate their spells. Instead, they know all of the spells from their chosen lore. The character may discard up to two of these spells in favour of up to two spells chosen from the Lore of Lustria or their lore's signature spell.

Note this Discipline cannot be combined with Wandering Deliberations.

wandering-deliberations.body:
Instead of generating spells normally, this character knows five signature spells chosen from the following Lores of Magic: Battle Magic, Daemonology, Dark Magic,

Elementalism, High Magic, Illusion and Necromancy. The character may discard up to two of these signature spells in favour of up to two spells from the Lore of Lustria (see page 21).

becalming-cogitation.body: Once per turn, the Slann Mage-Priest may re-roll one of the D6 when making a Wizardly dispel attempt. In addition, this character increases their Dispel range by 3".

sorcerous-void.body: This character gains the Magic Resistance (-D3) special rule. Roll the D3 before armies are deployed.

soul-of-stone.body:
The first time that a Slann suffers a Miscast, the spell fails

automatically, but no roll on the Miscast table is taken.

the-focused-rumination.body: This character may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Casting or Dispel rolls. In addition, this character can cast one more spell than is normal for their Level of Wizardry per turn.
